result.question: Examine the objectives and outcomes of Alauddin Khalji's market control and agrarian measures. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look into the issue in detail: its causes, effects and implications.

sentences.text: Contemporaries saw Alauddin Khalji's market control as a wonder of the world, and it was closely tied to his agrarian reforms.
The Mongol invasions forced him to keep a large army, which he could afford only if prices, and hence salaries, stayed low.
He set up three markets at Delhi, for foodgrains, costly cloth, and horses, slaves and cattle, each under an officer called the shahna.
Land revenue in the doab was collected directly by the state at half the produce, largely in cash, forcing peasants to sell grain cheaply to banjaras.
State warehouses stored grain for scarcity, and overcharging shopkeepers were harshly punished.
He was the first Sultan to assess land revenue in the doab by measurement.
The khuts and muqaddams had to pay the same taxes as others.
His market regulations outlived him and were retained by the Tughlaq sultans.
They helped him raise an efficient cavalry that repelled the Mongols.
His agrarian measures later provided a basis for the reforms of Sher Shah and Akbar.
